newsitem.title: USA: U.S. defense secretary's brother in shooting probe.
newsitem.headline: U.S. defense secretary's brother in shooting probe.

text.p: Police on Wednesday were investigating whether Defence Secretary William Cohen's older brother Robert acted in self-defence when he shot another man during a late-night altercation.

Police said Robert Cohen wounded Michael Chasse with a small-calibre handgun at Cohen's ranch-style home late on Tuesday night. Chasse, 22, was hit in the neck and was in fair condition at the Eastern Maine Medical Centre in Bangor.

"The central issue at this point is whether or not the homeowner, Robert Cohen, was justified in using the deadly force against the intruder Michael Chasse," Penobscot County District Attorney Christopher Almy said.

No charges have been filed in the case, and Brewer Police Chief Steve Barker said Cohen had been "fully cooperating" with investigators from Brewer and the Maine State Police. The probe will take time to complete, he said.
Almy and Barker said it was unclear if Cohen and Chasse knew each other, and could not say if other people were involved in the altercation but left the scene before police arrived.
"We're trying to determine what purpose Mr. Chasse had in being at the residence. How he knew Mr. Cohen and what all the circumstances were," Almy told reporters on Wednesday afternoon.
Cohen's lawyer was not available for comment.
Defence Secretary William Cohen faced questions about the incident throughout the day, including during a Pentagon photo opportunity with visiting Saudi Defence Minister Prince Sultan.

"As you all know from the wire reports, my brother last night experienced a rather unusual event -- an intruder," Cohen said. "My understanding is an intruder entered his home while armed with a knife and proceeded to attack him, and he defended himself."
The defence secretary, who has a law degree, said he acted as his brother's "surrogate attorney" during their telephone conversations. "My brother's doing fine. It was a very long night."
Police refused to confirm or deny reports that Chasse attacked Robert Cohen with a knife.

Chasse, from Lewiston, Maine, had been living recently in the Bangor-Brewer area. He is currently under indictment on a burglary charge and was convicted last year on charges connected with a high-speed chase, according to police and Almy.

Robert, who is William Cohen's older brother but whose exact age was unknown, worked in their father's bakery until it was sold last year. Robert Cohen was convicted earlier this month on drunken driving charges, according to authorities.

William Cohen, who like his brother is a native of Bangor, graduated from Boston University Law School in 1965 and represented Maine in the Senate and House of Representatives before becoming President Bill Clinton's defence secretary.
Barker and Almy refused to comment on whether they had been contacted by the Department of Defence.
"No comment, because the Bill Cohen factor really plays absolutely no part in this and I don't feel its appropriate to comment," Barker told reporters.
